caveats: traceability is tested against the page's own JSON twin first and then a bounded corpus of the newest 1200 results faces: an 'unsourced' number may still be a legitimate derived aggregate (a sum the page computes itself), so the unsourced list is a reading list, not a verdict
matching is half a unit of the last digit the page printed, so a rounded quote counts as sourced; a page that rounds harder than that will report the source as missing rather than match it
counts printed without a unit (a headcount, a session count) are sourced and acquitted on purpose -- the defect is a count wearing bp/pp/%

a defect requires the page to print a unit AND the cell that explains the value to carry a count word in its name; value coincidence is still possible for common small integers (a printed 20% cap can match an n_holdings of 20), so a hit is a candidate to read, not a proven error
an exact integer with no count word ('cpu_pct': 43.0) is filed as integral_under_a_unit, never as a defect: 43.0% is a real reading that merely lands on a whole number
only the newest page of each family is audited, and pages whose name ends in '-latest' are skipped as duplicates of the dated page beside them
identifiers inside backticks, dates, clock times and version strings are masked before tokenising: a six-digit code is not a number a reader quotes
this leg cannot tell whether a sourced number was rounded wrongly, only whether the cell it came from is a reading or a count
